title: No indication man in custody was suicidal
article: Police who arrested a Vancouver man who then hanged himself in a police wagon said the man gave no indication he was suicidal, and his last conversation was about how he was rooting for the Toronto Maple Leafs against the Canucks in a hockey game that night.
Gregory Douglas Lloyd, 43, died in hospital on Feb. 13, 2014, five days after he was found unresponsive in the back of the vehicle.
A coroner's inquest into his death began Tuesday.
Police were called after Lloyd used a set of keys to let himself into an apartment he used to share with a roommate in the 2100 block of Triumph Street in East Vancouver.
An assault occurred and the ex-roommate called police.

Lloyd was on bail for a previous crime at the time of the incident and was in breach of his bail conditions because he had a "no go" order forbidding him from being within a block of the residence. His bail conditions also included an order not to consume alcohol and Lloyd was intoxicated that night.
His police file had a "caution V," for violence on it and his ex-roommate warned the first officer who arrived, Sgt. Matthew Black, that Lloyd was "agitated and had a dislike for police."
But officers said they found a "calm, compliant" Lloyd.

Vancouver police Const. Steve Addison told the inquest when he arrived at the apartment Lloyd was sitting in a chair smoking a cigarette. "I waited until he was finished, he stood up and then I placed him in handcuffs," said Addison.
"There was nothing at all that led me to believe that Mr. Lloyd was going to be a risk to himself from self harm," he said.

Black said he waited outside about 35 minutes with the handcuffed Lloyd for the police wagon to arrive, during which time they discussed the Vancouver Canucks game that night. He talked about listening to the game once he got to the jail and they discussed Timothy Lake, where Black vacationed, and Lloyd said he was familiar with the area.
He also said he had a drinking problem and he hoped to get help for it in jail.
"There was no suicidal indication or action," Black told the coroner. "He was talking in the future tense."
A third officer, Vancouver police Const. Jocelyn Hetyie, said: "There was nothing to suggest he was a danger to himself or others."
Lloyd was found in the wagon with a ligature around his neck. He had a pulse but wasn't breathing.
Lloyd's mother and two other supporters were in the courtroom.
The four-person jury can make suggestions to try to prevent a similar death but do not assess blame or find cause.
